correctness.rationale: For all positive integers p,q, the bipartite adjacency block has precisely two distinct positive squared singular values and their negatives, plus an explicit zero leaf-space projector. The Schur-square sum reduces to two rank-one squared-profile matrices and leaf-block Schur squares. Leaf-block eigenvalues (s-1)/s and (s-2)/s, together with the hub-profile determinant (p-q)/(4 Delta), settle all boundary cases and yield matching explicit complete kernel bases. Independently reconstructed spectral projectors and 144 independent finite matrices corroborate the proof; finite tests are not used to establish universality.

value.rationale: The diameter-three double-star family is a recognized model for adjacency quantum state transfer. Its long-time mixing matrix has full rank precisely for distinct arm sizes at least three, despite an arbitrarily large zero-energy eigenspace. The theorem gives an exhaustive parameter boundary and explicit nullvectors for symmetric hubs, twin leaves and asymmetric singleton constraints, thereby resolving a natural complete classification rather than a chosen numeric example.
